record.original_question: Develop intrinsic methods for upper bounds on tensor subrank Q(T) and border subrank Q_bar(T) that do not proceed by upper-bounding these quantities through other rank notions.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Determine a genuine method for upper bounds on the subrank and border subrank of a tensor that does not rely on other notions of rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and let $T \in \mathbb{F}^{n_1} \otimes \mathbb{F}^{n_2} \otimes \mathbb{F}^{n_3}$ be a 3-tensor. The subrank $Q(T)$ is defined as the largest integer $r$ such that the diagonal tensor $\langle r \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^{r} e_i \otimes e_i \otimes e_i$ can be obtained from $T$ by applying linear maps to each of the three factors; equivalently, $Q(T) \geq r$ iff there exist linear maps $A_j : \mathbb{F}^{n_j} \to \mathbb{F}^r$ ($j=1,2,3$) such that $(A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes A_3)(T) = \langle r \rangle$. The border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ is the largest $r$ such that $\langle r \rangle$ lies in the Zariski closure of the orbit $\{(A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes A_3)(T) : A_j \in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{F}^{n_j}, \mathbb{F}^r)\}$ (working over an algebraically closed field, or in the corresponding topological sense over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$).

Known upper bounds on $Q(T)$ and $\underline{Q}(T)$ typically proceed indirectly: one bounds the subrank from above by another rank-type invariant of $T$ (for example, by the slice rank, analytic rank, geometric rank, partition rank, G-stable rank, or similar quantities) which is itself easier to control.

Problem: Develop a genuinely intrinsic method for proving upper bounds on the subrank $Q(T)$ and the border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ of a tensor $T$ that does not proceed by first upper-bounding $Q(T)$ or $\underline{Q}(T)$ by another rank notion of $T$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., border subrank via a generalised Hilbert–Mumford criterion, 2024; the Chang dissertation on border subrank, 2024) continues to develop techniques, but the standard upper bounds on subrank and border subrank still proceed via auxiliary rank notions (geometric rank, slice rank, etc.) or via the laser method. No source verifies that a fully intrinsic upper bound method has been established, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Border subrank via a generalised Hilbert-Mumford criterion
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers upper bound the dimension of the subrank ≥ r locus by estimating the rank of the derivative of a natural morphism parameterising the locus.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work introduces new geometric techniques for border subrank bounds, but they still rely on auxiliary geometric/rank-style invariants.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Rank of Tensors and Subrank of Matrix Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric rank upper bounds the (border) subrank: Q(T) ≤ GR(T).
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art upper bounds for subrank and border subrank are obtained via other rank notions such as geometric rank.

status_evidence.title: Border subrank of tensors (Chang dissertation, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies upper bounds on generic border subrank using geometric methods.
status_evidence.claim: Recent dissertation continues developing border subrank bounds via geometric/algebraic auxiliary invariants, indicating the intrinsic method problem remains open.
